doc.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016

title: Getting the Eastman job and his preparation as a teacher
summary: He was hired at Eastman after knowing Fred Sturm and Harold Danko, and found he needed more theory depth than his LA teaching had given him.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: This could be a hard question, but why — I would assume the position at Eastman, that you have, was a fairly competitive — I mean it’s a respected university throughout the world. So why did they pick you, do you think, as opposed to someone else?

I don’t know. I felt very lucky. I knew a few people there, that didn’t hurt. And I knew Fred Sturm who had been the head of the department there. I really was a fan of Harold Danko’s, who is the piano teacher still there. I had heard him with Thad Jones who was one of my favorites. So when I heard that — they called me. I didn’t know about the job. But I went and interviewed along with four other guys. So I felt pretty good about it. But it was a little bit of a rude awakening once I got there. I wasn’t really prepared when I got there in terms of being a teacher at Eastman. I’d taught a lot but I wasn’t as organized as I should have been.
Organization is a big part of it.
But where were you with the theoretical part of teaching jazz?

I was in a pretty good place with that. I’d been teaching a lot at some of the schools in Los Angeles — at USC and Cal Arts and I taught at a school called the Colburn School which is more of a classical school, and in terms of — well I don’t think you’re talking specifically like music theory, but I have a degree in music theory and so the theoretical, like harmony, like very specific harmony things, I was pretty good, I was pretty informed. But I’ve become a lot more informed. I realized how uninformed I was being at Eastman. Because my colleagues like Bill Dobbins and Jeff Campbell and Danko and there’s another guy called Dariusz Terefenko who — they’re just really informed. So I was pretty well informed but I think I had gotten much much more in depth with it, and that’s something I pass on to my students, really going for depth. Because I needed to go for more depth.
